doc.title: Zutty Singleton and Marge Singleton Interview, 1969-02-08

title: Jelly Roll's trio record and whether he used written parts
summary: Marge asks about the first trio record. Zutty says Jelly had only a lead sheet on the piano and that some things were written out.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: In the recording studio, the first record you made was... The trio, that's right. There was nothing written there, wasn't there?
No. He had some kind of lead sheet on the piano, you know, and he and Bonnie B. Garth would run over, things like that.
But all he wanted me to do was people, I wanted to listen and try to phrase it off.
But he didn't have no parts written on the Barney B. Garth. He'd have a little sort of a lead sheet on his piano name, and he's Barney B. Garth would run over, and, uh,
and spots of different things, and things like that. And the man, you know what?
Yeah, after G, where are we on?
Well, there are some things he had written.
What do you think did you do? That's the male people.
He implied that we left in our minds. This? Ha, ha, ha. Yum. And, uh, high society, and, uh,
Yeah, I'm sure. Yeah, I ought to take a look at that. Yeah.
I saw some of the, uh, but there was some music.
Oh, man. Yeah. When he rehearsed, if he had a score, say he had all parts written out.
Oh, that's me. Would you use those parts? I'm just playing with him.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
